names.inn: amfetamine (the racemate; EUDA, WHO ATC N06BA01, INCB); dexamfetamine is the INN of the (S)-enantiomer (EUDA, WHO ATC N06BA02, INCB)
names.iupac: α-methylbenzeneethanamine (systematic name given by EUDA); amphetamine is an α-methylphenethylamine

60-13-9: amphetamine sulfate, the most common salt (EUDA, read twice)
names.molar_mass: 135.2062 (NIST Chemistry WebBook, for amphetamine and, read twice, for dextroamphetamine); 135.2 (EUDA, no unit)
synonyms: Dexedrine (product name among NIST's other names)

forms.detail: EUDA: amfetamine is the racemic mixture of two enantiomers, formerly called d- and l- or (+) and (−) and now R and S; dexamfetamine (INN) is the (S)-enantiomer, (+)-α-methylphenethylamine, and levamfetamine the (R)-enantiomer. NIST lists dextroamphetamine (CAS 51-64-9; other names include (S)-amphetamine and (+)-amphetamine) as a stereoisomer of amphetamine.
The most common salt (CAS 60-13-9); a white or off-white powder, soluble in water.
A colourless volatile oil, insoluble in water.
EUDA: illicit products mostly consist of powders.
EUDA: tablets containing amphetamine may carry logos similar to those seen on MDMA and other ecstasy tablets.

INN lisdexamfetamine (WHO ATC N06BA12). The US label describes lisdexamfetamine dimesylate, chemically (2S)-2,6-diamino-N-[(1S)-1-methyl-2-phenylethyl] hexanamide dimethanesulfonate, molecular formula C15H25N3O∙(CH4O3S)2, molecular weight 455.60 (read twice), and states that 'Lisdexamfetamine is a prodrug of dextroamphetamine'. Marketed as Vyvanse capsules and chewable tablets (United States).
